walkthroughs.body_html:
Variation & Selection — a core area of GCSE Biology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Variation & Selection brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Variation & Selection.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: An organism with two different alleles at a locus is:
options: Homozygous
Heterozygous
Hemizygous
Polyploid

mcqs.q: A monohybrid cross of two heterozygotes Aa × Aa gives a phenotypic ratio (dominance) of:
How does a population of organisms become better adapted to its environment over time?
options: Individual organisms change during their lifetime in response to their environment and pass the changes on to offspring.
Individuals with advantageous heritable variations survive and reproduce more; their alleles increase in frequency over generations.
Organisms decide what features they need and grow them by force of will.
Only Na+ moves during an action potential; K+ stays still.

mcqs.q: Why are food chains usually limited to about 4 or 5 trophic levels?
options: There aren't enough types of animals to fill more trophic levels.
Larger animals always eat the next ones up, and there aren't enough giant animals.
Organisms decide what features they need and grow them by force of will.
Only ~10 percent of energy is transferred between trophic levels; eventually too little energy remains to support another level.

mcqs.q: During an action potential, do Na+ and K+ move through the same channels?
options: Larger animals always eat the next ones up, and there aren't enough giant animals.
Na+ and K+ swap places through the same channel at the same time.
Only Na+ moves during an action potential; K+ stays still.
No — voltage-gated Na+ channels open first (depolarisation, Na+ in), then voltage-gated K+ channels open (repolarisation, K+ out).

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Gene”?
options: Having two different alleles at a locus (e.g. Aa).
Having two identical alleles at a locus (e.g. AA or aa).
Observable characteristics resulting from interaction of genotype and environment.
Section of DNA coding for one polypeptide (or functional RNA); occupies a specific locus on a chromosome.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Heterozygous”?
options: Section of DNA coding for one polypeptide (or functional RNA); occupies a specific locus on a chromosome.
Differential survival and reproduction of organisms due to phenotypic variation; favourable alleles increase in frequency.
Having two different alleles at a locus (e.g. Aa).
Different version of a gene producing different forms of the same characteristic.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Phenotype”?
options: Having two identical alleles at a locus (e.g. AA or aa).
Differential survival and reproduction of organisms due to phenotypic variation; favourable alleles increase in frequency.
Observable characteristics resulting from interaction of genotype and environment.
Section of DNA coding for one polypeptide (or functional RNA); occupies a specific locus on a chromosome.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Homozygous”?
options: Different version of a gene producing different forms of the same characteristic.
Having two identical alleles at a locus (e.g. AA or aa).
Differential survival and reproduction of organisms due to phenotypic variation; favourable alleles increase in frequency.
Having two different alleles at a locus (e.g. Aa).

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Allele”?
options: Differential survival and reproduction of organisms due to phenotypic variation; favourable alleles increase in frequency.
Having two identical alleles at a locus (e.g. AA or aa).
Different version of a gene producing different forms of the same characteristic.
Having two different alleles at a locus (e.g. Aa).

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Natural selection”?
options: Having two identical alleles at a locus (e.g. AA or aa).
Differential survival and reproduction of organisms due to phenotypic variation; favourable alleles increase in frequency.
Observable characteristics resulting from interaction of genotype and environment.
Section of DNA coding for one polypeptide (or functional RNA); occupies a specific locus on a chromosome.

mcqs.q: In a population of beetles, those with darker colouring are better camouflaged from birds. Over many generations the population becomes mostly dark. This is an example of:
options: Natural selection
Selective breeding by humans
Inheritance of an acquired characteristic
A response with no genetic basis

mcqs.q: Identical twins raised in different countries differ in body mass. This difference is mainly due to:
options: Environmental factors
Genetic factors only
A mutation in one twin
Different numbers of chromosomes

mcqs.q: Two heterozygous parents (Bb × Bb) are crossed. What is the expected phenotypic ratio if B is dominant?
options: 3 dominant : 1 recessive
1 dominant : 1 recessive
All dominant

mcqs.q: A new allele appears in a population that was not present before. The most likely original source is:
options: A mutation in the DNA
The organism choosing to create it
The environment adding a gene
Loss of a chromosome

free_texts.q: Type the key term that means: "Different version of a gene producing different forms of the same characteristic."
free_texts.hint: It's one of the six key terms above.

sequence.def: Individuals differ due to random mutation
Survivors breed and pass on advantageous alleles
Over generations the species becomes better adapted
